newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher after rebound.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher after rebound.

text.p: COMEX copper settled firmer, largely pulled up by a sharp increase in the LME cash to three months premium or backwardation due to good borrowing of London's January contract, traders said.
Tightness from LME December was partly rolled to January, traders said.
LME backwardation rose from $50 to $55 overnight to level off at $88 to $92 by close of COMEX.
"Copper was getting oversold in the last few weeks and we had a nice rebound," said Fred Demler of E D and F Man International.
"Some of the selling we have seen from the Chinese dried up today and we saw a good amount of speculative shortcovering," Demler added.
March COMEX settled 2.20 cents firmer at 98.60 cents per pound, traded 99.40 to 96.50 cents. Spot December went out 2.25 cents higher at 101.05 cents.
Some traders saw the day's gains as being exaggerated by thin volume ahead of the year-end holidays.

With spot December COMEX back at a premium over cash LME, traders expected more "warehouse games" of metal moving from LME warehouses in the U.S. to their COMEX counterparts - a reversal of the trend in recent weeks when spot LME was briefly higher than December COMEX.
